title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 136
paragraphs: I commend this custom of theirs, and also the one next to be mentioned: namely that neither the king himself shall put anyone to death for a single cause, nor any of the other Persians for a single cause shall do irremediable harm to any of his own servants. Only if, after reckoning, he finds that the wrongs done are more in number and greater than the services rendered, does he then give vent to his anger. Moreover, they say that no one has ever killed his own father or mother, and whatever deeds have been done that seemed to be of this nature must necessarily, if examined, be found to be due either to changelings or to children of adulterous birth. For, they say, it is not reasonable to suppose that the true parent would be killed by his own son.
